```{r load}
# data from data-raw/wsg_vignette_data.R
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "flooded", mustWork = TRUE)
gpkg <- vd("pars.gpkg")
meta <- readRDS(vd("pars_meta.rds"))
present <- sf::st_layers(gpkg)$name
load_layer <- function(name) {
  if (name %in% present) sf::st_read(gpkg, layer = name, quiet = TRUE) else NULL
}
aoi <- load_layer("aoi")
# every layer clipped to the watershed group, so nothing draws outside it
clip <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) NULL else fresh::frs_clip(x, aoi)
streams <- clip(load_layer("streams"))
waterbodies <- clip(load_layer("waterbodies"))
roads <- clip(load_layer("roads"))
railways <- clip(load_layer("railways"))
reserves <- clip(load_layer("reserves"))
parks <- clip(load_layer("parks"))
named_streams <- clip(load_layer("named_streams"))
dem <- terra::mask(terra::crop(terra::rast(vd("pars_dem.tif")), terra::vect(aoi)), terra::vect(aoi))
valleys <- terra::mask(terra::crop(terra::rast(vd("pars_valleys.tif")), terra::vect(aoi)), terra::vect(aoi))

# the numbers the prose states
args <- meta$vca_args
ff <- args$flood_factor
cell_m <- terra::res(valleys)[1]
cell_ha <- prod(terra::res(valleys)) / 1e4
v_in <- terra::values(valleys)[, 1]
fp_cells <- sum(v_in == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)
fp_ha <- fp_cells * cell_ha
wsg_km2 <- aoi$area_ha / 100
stream_km <- sum(as.numeric(sf::st_length(streams))) / 1000
area_at <- meta$fp_area_ha
# lakes and wetlands, burned as fl_valley_confine() burns them (by cell centre)
wb_r <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(waterbodies), valleys, field = 1L, background = 0L)
wb_cell <- terra::values(wb_r)[, 1] == 1L & !is.na(v_in)
# the channel buffer fl_valley_confine() burns (half the channel width either side, by cell centre)
has_w <- !is.na(streams$channel_width) & streams$channel_width > 0
buf <- sf::st_buffer(streams[has_w, ], dist = streams$channel_width[has_w] / 2)
buf_cell <- terra::values(terra::rasterize(terra::vect(buf), valleys, field = 1L, background = 0L))[, 1] == 1L &
  !is.na(v_in)
sw <- meta$software
sw_row <- function(p) sw[sw$package == p, ]
commit_link <- function(p) {
  r <- sw_row(p)
  sprintf("[%s](https://github.com/%s/commit/%s)", substr(r$commit, 1, 7), r$repo, r$commit)
}
recompute_link <- sprintf("[%s](https://github.com/%s/commit/%s)", substr(sw_row("link")$commit_also, 1, 7),
                          sw_row("link")$repo, sw_row("link")$commit_also)
scen <- flooded::fl_scenarios()
fm <- formals(flooded::fl_valley_confine)

# formatting
n0 <- function(v) format(round(v), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
pc <- function(v, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * v, format = "f", digits = d), " %")
lst <- function(v) if (length(v) < 2) v else paste(paste(v[-length(v)], collapse = ", "), "and", v[length(v)])
# one value, present and not empty
has1 <- function(x) length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x) && nzchar(x)

# Each sentence below reads these as true; a rebuild that breaks one must change the prose.
stopifnot(
  # "streams of order 3 and up that bull trout can reach in link's default configuration"
  identical(meta$species, "BT"), identical(meta$link_config, "default"), isFALSE(meta$link_dirty),
  min(streams$stream_order) == 3, all(streams$access %in% c(1L, 2L)),
  # "every setting but the flood factor is the package default": what fl_valley_confine() itself defaults to
  all(names(args) %in% names(fm)),
  all(vapply(setdiff(names(args), "flood_factor"), function(a) isTRUE(args[[a]] == eval(fm[[a]])), logical(1))),
  # the call shown under "Data and how it was built" types flood_factor = 4
  ff == 4,
  # the answer is the area the build recorded for this flood factor, cell for cell
  identical(as.integer(fp_cells), meta$fp_cells[[as.character(ff)]]),
  # the three presets the article names, and the comparison with 7
  identical(as.numeric(scen$flood_factor), c(2, 4, 6)), "7" %in% names(area_at),
  area_at[["7"]] > area_at[[as.character(ff)]],
  # "it adds the lakes and wetlands": every lake and wetland cell inside the boundary is floodplain
  all(waterbodies$waterbody_type %in% c("L", "W")), all(v_in[wb_cell] == 1L),
  # "and the cells whose centre lies inside a stream's channel width": every one is floodplain
  all(v_in[buf_cell] == 1L), sum(buf_cell) > 0,
  # the software section's citations, and the run time's machine
  !anyNA(sw$release[sw$package != "fwapg"]), has1(sw_row("flooded")$concept_doi),
  has1(sw_row("link")$concept_doi), has1(sw_row("flooded")$doi_from),
  isFALSE(sw_row("flooded")$dirty), isFALSE(sw_row("link")$dirty), isFALSE(sw_row("link")$dirty_also),
  has1(meta$cpu), has1(meta$fwapg_read$read_at)
)
```

[`flooded`](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/flooded/) is an R package that maps floodplains
from an elevation model and a stream network. This article runs it over the Parsnip River
watershed group, `r n0(wsg_km2)` km² of British Columbia between Prince George and Mackenzie,
where the Parsnip River flows north into Williston Reservoir.

**The answer.** At flood factor `r ff`, `flooded` maps **`r n0(fp_ha)` ha of floodplain**,
`r pc(fp_ha / aoi$area_ha)` of the watershed group, along `r n0(stream_km)` km of streams of order
3 and up that bull trout can reach.

## What does the map show?

The map starts from the `r cell_m` m cells that pass four tests:

- the slope is at most `r args$slope_threshold` %;
- the cell is within `r n0(args$max_width / 2)` m of a stream in a straight line;
- it is close to a stream by a distance that counts steep ground as farther (a cost under
  `r n0(args$cost_threshold)`);
- it lies below a water level `r ff` times the stream's bankfull depth above the stream, spread
  across the valley from the streams. Bankfull depth is estimated from a stream's upstream area
  and mean annual precipitation, through Hall et al.'s regression for channel width
  [@hall_etal2007Predictingriver].

It then closes small gaps, fills holes under `r args$hole_threshold / 1e4` ha, drops patches under
`r args$size_threshold / 1e4` ha and smooths edges with a majority filter, so a cell can be in
without passing every test, or out despite passing them. Last, it adds the lakes and wetlands the
streams flow through, which make up `r pc(sum(wb_cell) / fp_cells)` of the floodplain, and the cells
whose centre lies inside a stream's channel width. Every setting but the flood factor is the
package default.

The streams are those of order 3 and up that bull trout can reach in the `default` configuration
of [`link`](`r sw_row("link")$url`), the R package that models fish access and habitat on BC's
stream network.

```{r map-floodplain, fig.cap = paste0("Floodplain at flood factor ", ff, " (green) over a hillshade of the elevation model, with the streams it was mapped from (blue), lakes and wetlands (pale green, outlined in blue), resource roads (grey), railways (black, dashed), parks and protected areas (light green), First Nations reserves (grey, marked with a diamond and named) and the watershed group boundary (black). Roads other than resource roads are left off at this scale.")}
hill <- terra::shade(
  terra::terrain(dem, "slope", unit = "radians"),
  terra::terrain(dem, "aspect", unit = "radians")
)
terra::plot(hill, col = grey(0:100 / 100), legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE, mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
terra::plot(valleys, col = c(NA, "#2c7a2c"), alpha = 0.55, add = TRUE, legend = FALSE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(waterbodies), col = "#a3cdb966", border = "#2171B5", lwd = 0.3, add = TRUE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(streams), col = "#1f77b4", lwd = 0.4, add = TRUE)
if (!is.null(roads)) {
  fsr <- roads[roads$transport_line_type_code %in% c("RRS", "RRD", "RRN"), ]
  if (nrow(fsr) > 0L) plot(sf::st_geometry(fsr), col = "#88888888", lwd = 0.25, add = TRUE)
}
if (!is.null(railways)) plot(sf::st_geometry(railways), col = "black", lwd = 0.8, lty = "dashed", add = TRUE)
# land-use polygons above hydro and transport, so they read where they overlap;
# colours from the gq registry (reg_qgis_restoration.json)
if (!is.null(parks)) plot(sf::st_geometry(parks), col = "#639b5f55", border = "#33a02c", lwd = 0.7, add = TRUE)
label_reserves <- function(r, cex_pt) {
  pts <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(r), of_largest_polygon = TRUE))
  plot(pts, pch = 23, bg = "#222222", col = "white", cex = cex_pt, add = TRUE)
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(pts)
  ly <- xy[, 2] - par("cxy")[2] * 0.45 * 0.9
  hx <- par("cxy")[1] * 0.45 * 0.05
  hy <- par("cxy")[2] * 0.45 * 0.05
  # a thin white halo, then the label; xpd so a label near the edge is not cut off
  for (d in list(c(-1, 0), c(1, 0), c(0, -1), c(0, 1))) {
    text(xy[, 1] + d[1] * hx, ly + d[2] * hy, labels = r$english_name, cex = 0.45, col = "white",
         font = 2, xpd = TRUE)
  }
  text(xy[, 1], ly, labels = r$english_name, cex = 0.45, col = "#111111", font = 2, xpd = TRUE)
}
if (!is.null(reserves)) {
  plot(sf::st_geometry(reserves), col = "#b2b2b288", border = "#232323", lwd = 0.6, add = TRUE)
}
plot(sf::st_geometry(aoi), border = "black", lwd = 1.5, add = TRUE)
if (!is.null(reserves) && nrow(reserves) > 0L) label_reserves(reserves, 0.9)
```

## Which flood level should I use?

`flooded` has three preset levels: 2, 4 and 6 times bankfull depth. A factor of 2 follows Rosgen's
definition of flood-prone width, twice the maximum bankfull depth, which roughly matches a 50-year flood
stage or less
[@nagel_etal2014LandscapeScale]. `flooded` calls 4 the functional floodplain and 6 the valley
bottom; those names are its own reading, not a published one. This article uses `r ff`. For valley
extent on 30 m elevation models, Nagel et al. found a factor of 7 the most appropriate.

With every other setting unchanged, the Parsnip's floodplain is `r lst(paste(n0(area_at), "ha"))`
at flood factors `r lst(names(area_at))`. Going from `r ff` to 7 adds
`r pc(area_at[["7"]] / area_at[[as.character(ff)]] - 1)`.

## How do I read it up close?

The south-east corner holds the Parsnip's headwaters around Arctic Lake, on the divide between
Arctic and Pacific drainage. At this scale the floodplain follows individual channels, lakes and
wetlands, and sits against roads, railways, reserves and parks.

The map does not record which test, or which step of the tidying, left a cell out.

```{r map-detail, fig.cap = "The south-east corner of the watershed group, around Arctic Lake: floodplain (green), streams (blue) with named streams labelled, lakes and wetlands (pale green, outlined in blue), roads and trails (grey), railways (black, dashed), parks and protected areas (light green) and First Nations reserves (grey, named)."}
e <- sf::st_bbox(aoi)
inset_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(c(
  xmin = unname(e["xmin"] + (e["xmax"] - e["xmin"]) * 0.55),
  ymin = unname(e["ymin"]),
  xmax = unname(e["xmax"]),
  ymax = unname(e["ymin"] + (e["ymax"] - e["ymin"]) * 0.45)
), crs = sf::st_crs(streams))
inset_ext <- terra::ext(inset_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax", "ymin", "ymax")])
crop_sf <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0L) return(NULL)
  out <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_crop(x, inset_bbox))
  if (nrow(out) == 0L) NULL else out
}
dem_i <- terra::crop(dem, inset_ext)
hill_i <- terra::shade(
  terra::terrain(dem_i, "slope", unit = "radians"),
  terra::terrain(dem_i, "aspect", unit = "radians")
)
terra::plot(hill_i, col = grey(0:100 / 100), legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE, mar = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
terra::plot(terra::crop(valleys, inset_ext), col = c(NA, "#2c7a2c"), alpha = 0.55, add = TRUE, legend = FALSE)
wb_i <- crop_sf(waterbodies)
if (!is.null(wb_i)) plot(sf::st_geometry(wb_i), col = "#a3cdb988", border = "#2171B5", lwd = 0.4, add = TRUE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(crop_sf(streams)), col = "#1f77b4", lwd = 0.7, add = TRUE)
roads_i <- crop_sf(roads)
if (!is.null(roads_i)) plot(sf::st_geometry(roads_i), col = "#666666aa", lwd = 0.4, add = TRUE)
rail_i <- crop_sf(railways)
if (!is.null(rail_i)) plot(sf::st_geometry(rail_i), col = "black", lwd = 1.0, lty = "dashed", add = TRUE)
parks_i <- crop_sf(parks)
if (!is.null(parks_i)) plot(sf::st_geometry(parks_i), col = "#639b5f55", border = "#33a02c", lwd = 0.8, add = TRUE)
res_i <- crop_sf(reserves)
if (!is.null(res_i)) plot(sf::st_geometry(res_i), col = "#b2b2b2aa", border = "#232323", lwd = 0.7, add = TRUE)
aoi_i <- crop_sf(aoi)
if (!is.null(aoi_i)) plot(sf::st_geometry(aoi_i), border = "black", lwd = 1.5, add = TRUE)
ns_i <- crop_sf(named_streams)
if (!is.null(ns_i)) {
  # one label per name, at the middle of its first segment
  dedup <- ns_i[!duplicated(ns_i$gnis_name), ]
  pts <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(dedup)))
  text(sf::st_coordinates(pts), labels = dedup$gnis_name, cex = 0.5, font = 3, col = "#0d3a6c")
}
if (!is.null(res_i)) label_reserves(res_i, 1.0)
```

## How good is it?

This map has not been compared with floodplain mapped on the ground. Its water level rests on Hall
et al.'s channel-width regression, which explains about half the variation in width (R² = 0.47)
across 1,951 field measurements in the Columbia River basin [@hall_etal2007Predictingriver], and on a conversion
from width to depth fitted in a single Idaho basin. The flood factor multiplies whatever error those
carry.

## What should you know before using it?

- **It maps terrain, not floods.** No discharge, flood routing or return period goes into it; the
  flood factor sets a level relative to the streams' bankfull depth.
- **It starts only from the streams it is given.** A smaller stream, or one bull trout cannot reach,
  does not seed the map; ground beside it is in the map only as measured from those streams, through
  the tidying, or as part of a lake or wetland they flow through.
- **It works on `r cell_m` m cells.** Nothing narrower than a cell is resolved.

## Data and how it was built

The elevation model is Natural Resources Canada's
[MRDEM-30](https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/18752265-bda3-498c-a4ba-9dfe68cb98da). The
streams are BC Freshwater Atlas segments from `link`'s run of `r meta$link_run_date`, with upstream
area and mean annual precipitation from [fwapg](`r sw_row("fwapg")$url`); lakes, wetlands and
named streams are from the atlas too. Roads and trails, railways, reserves, and parks and protected
areas are from the BC Data Catalogue. The data were built by
[`data-raw/wsg_vignette_data.R`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/flooded/blob/main/data-raw/wsg_vignette_data.R),
which ran the call below; the `fl_valley_confine()` call took `r round(meta$vca_seconds / 60, 1)` minutes
(`r meta$cpu`):

```{r vca, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
valleys <- flooded::fl_valley_confine(
  dem = dem,
  streams = streams,
  area_field = "upstream_area_ha",
  precip = flooded::fl_stream_rasterize(streams, dem, field = "map_upstream"),
  waterbodies = waterbodies,
  flood_factor = 4
)
```

The results can be downloaded:
[`pars.gpkg`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/flooded/raw/main/inst/vignette-data/pars.gpkg)
(the floodplain, streams, lakes and wetlands, and the map layers),
[`pars_valleys.tif`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/flooded/raw/main/inst/vignette-data/pars_valleys.tif)
(the floodplain grid) and
[`pars_dem.tif`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/flooded/raw/main/inst/vignette-data/pars_dem.tif)
(the elevation model, truncated to whole metres; the floodplain was mapped from the unrounded values).

## Software and how to cite it

- [`flooded`](`r sw_row("flooded")$url`) `r sw_row("flooded")$release`, at commit
  `r commit_link("flooded")`: the floodplain model. DOI
  [`r sw_row("flooded")$concept_doi`](https://doi.org/`r sw_row("flooded")$concept_doi`).
- [`link`](`r sw_row("link")$url`) `r sw_row("link")$release`, modelled at commit
  `r commit_link("link")` and recomputed at `r recompute_link`: which streams bull trout can reach.
  DOI [`r sw_row("link")$concept_doi`](https://doi.org/`r sw_row("link")$concept_doi`).
- [`fresh`](`r sw_row("fresh")$url`) `r sw_row("fresh")$release`, at commit `r commit_link("fresh")`:
  the stream network modelling engine `link` runs on.
- [fwapg](`r sw_row("fwapg")$url`), at commit `r commit_link("fwapg")` as `link`'s run recorded it: the
  Freshwater Atlas in PostgreSQL. Upstream area and precipitation were read from its tables on
  `r substr(meta$fwapg_read$read_at, 1, 10)`.

Cite `flooded` as:

```{r cite, results = "asis"}
cat(format(utils::citation("flooded"), style = "text"), sep = "\n\n")
```

and by its DOI, which covers its releases from `r sw_row("flooded")$doi_from` on and resolves to the
latest:
<https://doi.org/`r sw_row("flooded")$concept_doi`>.
